PCA, tsne, umap), data formatting conversions packages programs, population structure, genetic prediction, private allele detection (See documentation details). functions written take similar arguments interpret consistent ways. done use snpRdata object class, snpR functions take first argument. Nearly functions written overwrite safe: object provided function overwritten output. Newly calculated statistics simply merged-existing object. fundamental feature snpR use facets. Facets define categorical metadata features data, can reference either features describing individual SNPs (chromosome) individual samples (population). Facets used automatically break apart input data calculate statistics intuitive ways, calculating observed heterozygosity population. title: Introduction to Basic SNP Analysis with snpR
text: snpR can take variety SNP data formats. basic input format tab-delimited SNP dataset, row contains metadata genotypes single SNP. Genotypes noted two characters, “GG” “GA” G/G homozygote G/heterozygote, respectively. missing data format can user-defined, “NN” default. example, see stick_NN_input.txt distributed package. Note identical format output , example, ANGSD software package. Ensure genotypes stored factors import. resulting data looks like: Note snpR can also import data genotypes stored four numbers (ex. “GG”, “GA”, “NN” “0101”, “0102”, “0000”, respectively), single numeric character represents count minor allele (0 2 homozygotes, 1 heterozygotes). Data “NN” format, shown , can imported directly snpRdata set alongside corresponding metadata using import.snpR.data function: Note: Column names snp sample metadata must unique (repeats across metadata sets), contain ‘.’, ‘~’, whitespace! functions expect see columns named ‘chr’ ‘position’. Ensuring snp.meta columns early saves potential column renaming later. Shared metadata levels across different columns can cause issues statistics calculated two categories (example, population family named “”). existing objects adegenet genind genlight format, vcfR format, vcf file, plink files, FSTAT file, genepop file, can also automatically imported! Look “read_vcf()” “convert_genind()” style functions. delimited genotype formats (NN 0000) can also automatically imported read_delimited_snps() function.
code: NNfile <- system.file("extdata", "stick_NN_input.txt", package = "snpR") ##       chr position ASP.r2.141 ASP.r2.144 ASP.r2.146 ASP.r2.147 ## 1  groupI 10593829         GG         GG         GG         GG ## 2  groupI 16498302         TT         TT         CT         TT ## 3  groupI 19759331         AA         NN         GG         NN ## 4  groupI 21284266         GG         GG         GG         NN ## 5  groupI 22746027         GG         GG         GG         GG ## 6 groupII 10829169         CC         CC         CC         CG # the first three characters of the column names are the population, so let's grab that. # since the first three columns contain snp.metadata, we need to remove those before import! sample_meta <- data.frame(pop = substr(colnames(NN[-c(1:2)]), 1, 3), stringsAsFactors = F)  # grab our sample metadata snp_meta <- NN[,1:2]  # grab the genetic data gen_data <- NN[,3:ncol(NN)]  # import, remember to remove metadata from the genotypes! my.dat <- import.snpR.data(genotypes = gen_data,                             snp.meta = snp_meta,                             sample.meta = sample_meta) my.dat2 <- read_delimited_snps(NNfile, sample.meta = sample_meta, header_cols = 2) identical(my.dat, my.dat2) ## [1] TRUE

text: snpRdata objects store range variables internally order minimize repeat computation things like allele frequencies. Calling snpRdata object show summary calculations done object metadata categories available. large, snpRdata objects accessed via accessor functions: snpRdata objects can subset using usual bracket operators, specifying first snps keep, samples keep: Almost snpR functions built allow overwriting easy object management. Since calculated data stored snpRdata objects, snpR functions generally return snpRdata object given , extra data merged . example, calculate observed heterozygosity, calc_ho function can used: Calculated statistics can fetched using get.snpR.stats accessor function. Note function returns data.frame nested list (depending requested stats), snpRdata object, never used overwrite snpRdata object!. Since calculations run pairwise need specify want pairwise single stats returned. get.snpR.stats automatically return multiple types data available. Typically, statistic calculated within individual snp weighted averages within populations (facet levels).
code: my.dat # get the number of samples nsamps(my.dat) ## [1] 100 ncol(my.dat) ## [1] 100 # get the number of SNPs nsnps(my.dat) ## [1] 100 nrow(my.dat) ## [1] 100 # dim also works dim(my.dat) ## [1] 100 100 # view sample metadata head(sample.meta(my.dat)) ##   pop .sample.id ## 1 ASP          1 ## 2 ASP          2 ## 3 ASP          3 ## 4 ASP          4 ## 5 ASP          5 ## 6 ASP          6 # write to sample metadata; note that writing to any part of the metadata or genotypes will cause any calculations # to be discarded, since the new columns can cause some unexpected results. sample.meta(my.dat)$fam <- sample(LETTERS[1:4], nsamps(my.dat), T)  # view snp metadata head(snp.meta(my.dat)) ##          chr position .snp.id ## 1    groupVI   212436       1 ## 2 groupXVIII   350070       2 ## 3    groupXV   854285       3 ## 4  groupXIII   907279       4 ## 5    groupVI  1068620       5 ## 6     groupV  1392753       6 # write to sample metadata; note that writing to any part of the metadata or genotypes will cause any calculations # to be discarded, since the new columns can cause some unexpected results. snp.meta(my.dat)$new_snp_col <- sample(LETTERS[1:6], nsnps(my.dat), T) ## Warning in validityMethod(object): Some levels are duplicated across multiple sample meta facets. ## This will cause issues if those sample facets are run during analysis. ## Issues: ##  ## Level: A in facets: fam, new_snp_col ## Level: B in facets: fam, new_snp_col ## Level: C in facets: fam, new_snp_col ## Level: D in facets: fam, new_snp_col snp.meta(my.dat)$new_snp_col <- NULL  # view genotypes, can be written to as above genotypes(my.dat)[1:6, 1:6] ## 3         CC         CC         CC         CC         CC         CC ## 4         AA         AA         AA         AA         AG         AA ## 5         GG         NN         NN         AA         GG         AG ## 6         AC         AC         AA         AA         AA         AC sub1 <- my.dat[1:10,] nsnps(sub1) ## [1] 10 sub2 <- my.dat[,1:10] nsamps(sub2) ## [1] 10 # calculate observed heterozygosity, overwriting the my.dat object my.dat <- calc_ho(my.dat) # fetch calculated statistics ho <- get.snpR.stats(my.dat, stats = "ho") head(ho$single) ## 4 .base    .base  groupXIII   907279       4 0.44318182 ## 5 .base    .base    groupVI  1068620       5 0.38983051 ## 6 .base    .base     groupV  1392753       6 0.35483871 head(ho$weighted.means) ##   facet subfacet snp.facet snp.subfacet weighted_mean_ho ## 1 .base    .base     .base        .base        0.3171868

title: Introduction to Basic SNP Analysis with snpR
text: Facets defined reference column names either snp sample metadata provided creating snpRdata object. example, facet “pop” split .dat apart pop column sample metadata run requested function calculation levels/subfacets within facet (eg. facet pop comprises 6 levels/subfacets - ASP, CLF, OPL, PAL, SMR, UPD). Whereas facet “chr” split .dat apart “chr” column snp metadata (21 levels/subfacets) run specified calculation unique level/subfacet. calculate observed heterozygosity SNP within population, example, one can supply “pop” facet.
code: my.dat <- calc_ho(my.dat, facets = "pop") #running the calculation head(get.snpR.stats(my.dat, facets = "pop", stats = "ho")$weighted.means) #retrieving the results ##   facet subfacet snp.facet snp.subfacet weighted_mean_ho ## 1   pop      ASP     .base        .base        0.3419156 ## 2   pop      CLF     .base        .base        0.2970480 ## 3   pop      OPL     .base        .base        0.3446866 ## 4   pop      PAL     .base        .base        0.2136752 ## 5   pop      SMR     .base        .base        0.3265910 ## 6   pop      UPD     .base        .base        0.3660377

Let’s go example produce simple COLONY input file. example individuals run potential siblings COLONY. Preparing COLONY candidate parents requires preparation knowledge dataset.
code: # Note: code not run for simplicity write_colony_input(x = stickSNPs, outfile = "sticksnps1.dat", sampleIDs = .sample.id, seed = 4562) # a more complex example requires 1) creating and adding variables to the stickSNPs example dataset and 2) creating more snpR objects. # Note: code not run for simplicity  # first creating new variables for the dataset  a <- 2013:2015 # possible birthyears b <- c("M", "F", "U") # possible sexes stk <- stickSNPs # new snpR object to manipulate sample.meta(stk)$BirthYear <- sample(x = a, size = nsamps(stk), replace = TRUE) # create birthyears sample.meta(stk)$ID <- 1:nsamps(stk) # create unique sampleID sample.meta(stk)$Sex <- sample(x= b, size = nsamps(stk), replace = TRUE) # create sexes  # generating snpR objects for male and female potential parents and offspring (selecting only inds with "known" sex) lsir <- which(stk@sample.meta$Sex =="M" & stk@sample.meta$BirthYear == "2013") # list of sires ldam <- which(stk@sample.meta$Sex =="F" & stk@sample.meta$BirthYear == "2013") # list of dams loff <- which(stk@sample.meta$BirthYear %in% c("2014","2015")) # list of offspring  # creating new snpR objects for Colony formatting sir <- subset_snpR_data(x = stk, .samps = lsir)  dam <- subset_snpR_data(x = stk, .samps = ldam) off <- subset_snpR_data(x = stk, .samps = loff)  # ok, now ready to write colony input write_colony_input(x = off, maternal_genotypes = dam, paternal_genotypes = sir, outfile = "sticksnps2.dat", seed = 5674) # see the documentation for write_colony_input for details on more options

text: calc_pi(): Nucleotide diversity. calc_ho(): Observed heterozygosity. calc_he(): Expected heterosygosity. calc_hwe(): Hardy-Weinburg equilibrium (HWE). calc_het_hom_ratios(): Alternative, raw heterozygote/homozygote ratios within individuals. calc_ne(): Effective population size. calc_prop_poly(): proportion polymorphic loci. calc_maf(): Minor allele frequencies, calculated automatically facet operations performed. calc_private(): Rarefaction-corrected detection private alleles across facet levels. calc_seg_sites(): Rarefaction-corrected estimates number segregating sites per facet level. calc_allelic_richness():: Rarefaction-corrected estimates allele counts per locus per facet level. calc_genetic_distances(): Genetic distances individuals. calc_fis(): FISF_{} (inbreeding coefficients). calc_roh(): Run--Homozygosity detection FROHF_{ROH} calculation. calc_pairwise_fst(): Pairwise FSTF_{ST} facet levels. calc_global_fst(): Global FSTF_{ST} across facet levels. calc_pairwise_ld(): Pairwise LD SNPs. calc_abba_baba(): ABBA/BABA tests. calc_tajimas_d(): Tajima’s D globally (across windows). Also calculates Watterson’s Tajima’s θ\theta. calc_association(): Association testing phenotype. run_random_forest(): Run random forest prediction/association test phenotype. cross_validate_genomic_prediction(): Bare-bones cross-validation genomic predictions. make_sfs(): Wrapper function uses external dadi formatted file generate sfs. calc_directionality(): Peter Slatkin’s directionality index. calc_origin_of_expansion(): Estimate origin point range expansion based directionality. calc_isolation_by_distance(): Run IBD mantel test. calc_tree(): Generate tree based individual facet-level relatedness. tabulate_allele_frequency_matrix(): Generate allele frequency matrix.

text: snpR also facilitates ease--use overwrite safe. , new analyses added existing object. Results can fetched using get.snpR.stats handler. Functions snpR consistently named: functions calculate statistics prefixed calc_, functions plots prefixed plot_, functions run external tools (like COLONY), named run_. code: library(snpR) ## basic example code  x <- calc_ho(stickSNPs, facets = c("pop")) # split by pop (stickSNPs is an example dataset included in snpR) x <- calc_ho(x, facets = c("fam")) # split by family x <- calc_ho(x, facets = c("pop.fam")) # split by combinations of family and pop res <- get.snpR.stats(x, facets = "pop", stats = "ho")

title: Conduct an ABBA/BABA test for gene flow. — calc_abba_baba
text: ABBA/BABA test according Green et al (2010) tests hypothesis equal number loci population 1 population 2  closely related population 3. ratio two scenarios given ABBA/BABA, : ABBA = (1 - p1)p2p3 BABA = p1(1 - p2)p3. p1, p2, p3 derived allele frequencies populations 1 3, respectively. D values provided overall comparison within levels provided snp facets. p-values D can calculated block jackknifing approach according Maier et. al (2022) removing SNPs n genomic windows (blocks) calculating D sites. Non-overlapping windows "blocked" reference provided SNP metadata facets (usually chromosome), length equal sigma, providing sigma = 100 use 100kb windows.

title: Run case/control or quantitative association tests on SNP data. — calc_association
text: Runs several different association tests SNP data. response variable must two different categories (case/control) test types, although "gmmat.score" method supports quantitative traits. Tests may broken sample-specific facets.

title: Run case/control or quantitative association tests on SNP data. — calc_association
code: calc_association(   x,   facets = NULL,   response,   method = "gmmat.score",   w = c(0, 1, 2),   formula = NULL,   family.override = FALSE,   maxiter = 500,   sampleID = NULL,   Gmaf = 0,   par = FALSE,   cleanup = TRUE,   verbose = FALSE )

title: Run case/control or quantitative association tests on SNP data. — calc_association
text: x snpRdata object facets character, default NULL. Categorical metadata variables break analysis. See Facets_in_snpR details. response character. Name column containing response variable interest. Must match column name sample metadata. Response must categorical, two categories. method character, default "gmmat.score". Specifies association method. Options: gmmat.score: Population/family structure corrected mlm approach, based Chen et al (2016). armitage: Armitage association test, based Armitage (1955). odds_ratio: Log odds ratio test. chisq: Chi-squared test. See description details. w numeric, default c(0, 1, 2). Weight variable genotype Armitage association method. See description details. formula character, default set response ~ 1. Null formula response variable, described formula. family.override character, default NULL. Provides alternative model family object use GMMAT GWAS regression. default, uses gaussian, link = "identity" quantitative phenotype binomial, link = "logit" categorical phenotype. maxiter numeric, default 500. Maximum iterations use fitting glmm using gmmat.score option. sampleID character, default NULL. Optional, name column sample metadata use sampleID using gmmat.score option. Gmaf numeric, default NULL. using "GMMAT" option, can provide optional minor allele frequency filter used constructing relatedness matrix. par numeric FALSE, default FALSE. Number parallel cores use computation. cleanup logical, default TRUE. TRUE, files produced "gmmat" option removed completion. verbose Logical, default FALSE. TRUE, progress updates printed console.

title: Run case/control or quantitative association tests on SNP data. — calc_association
text: snpRdata object resulting association test results merged stats socket.

title: Run case/control or quantitative association tests on SNP data. — calc_association
text: Several methods can used: Armitage, chi-squared, odds ratio. Armitage approach weights provided "w" argument, specifies weight possible genotype (homozygote 1, heterozygote, homozygote 2). default, c(0,1,2), specifies additive model. "gmmat.score" method uses approach described Chen et al. (2016) implemented glmmkin glmm.score functions. method, 'G' genetic relatedness matrix first created using Gmatrix function according Yang et al 2010. Multi-category data currently supported, development. Facets specified described Facets_in_snpR. NULL "" facet specifications function described. Note individuals one facet level one two possible phenotypes, association test return NA NaN. result, response variable overlaps perfectly facet variable, results NA NaN. chisq method used, column also returned specifies allele (major minor) associated phenotype.

title: Generate bootstrapped windowed statistics — do_bootstraps
text: x snpRdata object. facets character NULL, default NULL. Categories break bootstraps. boots numeric. Number bootstraps generate. sigma numeric. Designates width windows kilobases. Full window size 6*sigma. step numeric NULL, default default 2*sigma (non-overlapping windows). Designates number kilobases window centroid. NULL, windows centered SNP. statistics character. Designates statistic(s) smooth, typically "", "single", "pairwise". See details options. nk logical, default TRUE. TRUE, weights SNP contribution window averages number observations SNPs. par numeric FALSE, default FALSE. numeric, number cores use parallel processing. triple_sigma Logical, default FALSE. TRUE, sigma tripled create windows 6*sigma total. gaussian Logical, default TRUE. TRUE, windows gaussian smoothed. , windows raw averages. .p logical, default TRUE. Determines p-values calculated sliding windows. p.alt character, default "two-sided". Specifies alternative hypothesis used. Options: "less": probability bootstrapped value small smaller observed. "greater": probability bootstrapped value large larger observed. "two-sided": probability bootstrapped value extreme observed.

title: Pull calculated statistics from snpRdata objects. — get.snpR.stats
text: single: non-pairwise, non-window statistics (pi, ho, etc.) pairwise: pairwise, non-window statistics (Fst). single.window: non-pairwise, sliding window statistics. pairwise.window: pairwise, sliding window statistics. LD: linkage disequilibrium matrices tables. bootstraps: bootstraps window statistics. genetic_distance: genetic distances allele_frequency_matrix: allele frequency matrices. geo_dist: geographic distances. ibd: isolation distance results. sample: sample stats. pop: population summary statistics. weighted.means: Weighted means SNP statistics per facet level.

title: Pull calculated statistics from snpRdata objects. — get.snpR.stats
text: ho: Observed heterozygosity, via calc_ho. pi: pi (expected number pairwise differences, via calc_pi). maf: minor allele frequencies (major/minor counts identities), via calc_maf. private: private allele identities, via calc_private. association: results phenotypic association tests, via calc_association. hwe: Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium p-values, via calc_hwe. tajimas_d: Tajima's D, Watterson's Theta, Tajima's Theta, via calc_tajimas_d. fst: Pairwise Fst, via calc_pairwise_fst. het_hom_ratio: Heterozygote/Homozygote ratios within individuals, via calc_het_hom_ratio. ne: Effective population size estimates, via calc_ne. ld: Pairwise linkage disequilibrium, via calc_pairwise_ld. genetic_distances: Genetic distances, calc_genetic_distances. isolation_by_distance: Genetic isolation distance metrics, via calc_isolation_by_distance. geographic_distance: Geographic distances samples–use genetic data. Calculated calc_isolation_by_distance, fetchable independently . random_forest: Random forest snp-specific responses, see run_random_forest.

title: Import genotype and metadata into a snpRdata object. — import.snpR.data
text: Genotypes, metadata, results stored slots directly accessable '' symbol operator. Slots follows: sample.meta: sample metadata (population, family, phenotype, etc.). snp.meta: SNP metadata (SNP ID, chromosome, linkage group, position, etc.). facet.meta: internal metadata used track facets previously applied dataset. mDat:missing data format. snp.form: number characters per SNP. genotables: list containing tabulated genotypes (gs), allele counts (), missing data (wm). facet.meta contains corresponding metadata. facets: vector facets added data. facet.type: classes added facets (snp, sample, complex, .base). stats:  data.frame containing calculated non-pairwise single-snp statistics metadata. window.stats: data.frame/table containing non-pairwise statistics calculated sliding windows. pairwise.stats: data.frame/table containing pairwise (fst) single-snp statistics. pairwise.window.stats: data.frame/table containing pairwise statistics calculated sliding windows. sample.stats:  data.frame/table containing statistics calculated individual sample. pairwise.LD:nested list containing linkage disequilibrium data (see calc_pairwise_ld information). window.bootstraps: data.frame/table containing calculated bootstraps sliding window statistics. sn: list containing "sn", sn formatted data, "type" type interpolation. calced_stats: Named list named character vectors tracks calculated statistics facet (see calc_genetic_distances information). genetic_distances: nested list containing genetic distance data. names: column names genotypes. row.names: row names genotypes. .Data: list vectors containing raw genotype data. .S3Class: notes inherited S3 object class. Note slots used primarily internally. calculated data can accessed using get.snpR.stats function. See documentation.
